blocks.text: Condo buildings in Downtown VW

"Downtown West Vancouver" would be wrong — West Vancouver is a different municipality. The City of Vancouver has only ONE Downtown local area, one of its 22 distinct areas; "VW" is a board/site distinction, not a City one. (5) Fairmont Pacific Rim Residences and the Paradox Residences are filed under Coal Harbour per their board sub-area, not here. (6) This list is a selective set of verified named towers labelled Downtown VW in their sources, stated openly — it is not a census.
The Private Residences at Hotel Georgia — 667 Howe Street

A 48-storey tower beside the historic 1927 Hotel Georgia: 156 luxury condominiums on floors 14 to 48 above office and hotel floors, completed in 2012 per current listings and the building's project history (a building directory records built 2013 — flagged, not resolved; 2012 is used here). Listings record Freehold Strata title, concrete and glass construction, and Downtown VW sub-area. The building directory records the strata bylaws as: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed — the rental line is in any event governed by the post-2022 law in.
Tate Downtown (Tate on Howe) — 1283 Howe Street
Strata Plan EPP30416. A townhouse unit at the building's base is documented in the townhome subsection below. Published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
1188 Howe — 1188 Howe Street

Strata Plan LMS1468, at Howe and Davie. The building directory's description records a 28-level concrete building with 185 residential units and 5 commercial units, while its own FAQ records 190 units in total and built 1995 against a description line of built 1994 — both pairs are flagged as internally conflicted, not resolved. A current listing describes the building as pets allowed.
Spectrum 1 — 111 West Georgia Street (Concord Pacific)

A current listing records Spectrum 1 by Concord Pacific, year built 2007, Downtown VW sub-area, with city, mountain and BC Place views. Unit count and published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
Streets, schools and getting around Downtown VW

items.t: Downtown VW is the downtown peninsula's Vancouver West board side: the central business district and the Georgia / Granville / Burrard / Robson core, on Burrard Inlet's south shore. The City describes the containing Downtown local area as a peninsula bounded by Burrard Inlet on the north, False Creek and Yaletown to the south, the West End and Stanley Park to the west, and Gastown, Chinatown and Strathcona to the east; a board-published boundary for Downtown VW alone: UNVERIFIED.
Detached houses are not a VW-core housing form.

Main streets: West Georgia Street, Granville Street, Burrard Street and Howe Street. The City's Downtown history names Georgia and Granville Streets as the city-centre streets the centre moved up to from Water and Cordova Streets after incorporation.

Transit anchors: the core is the hub where the Expo Line, Millennium Line and Canada Line meet (Waterfront and Burrard stations); the R5 Hastings St RapidBus terminates at Burrard Station, route 22 also runs from Burrard Station, and route 50 starts at Waterfront Station and runs via Chinatown, Granville Island and the False Creek south shore to Olympic Village Station.

Civic anchors in the core: Vancouver Public Library Central Library, 350 West Georgia Street, and St. Paul's Hospital, 1081 Burrard Street — a Providence Health Care hospital, not a Vancouver Coastal Health site.

blocks.text: Good to know about Downtown VW

items.t: The city centre moved uphill, and the VW core is where it landed. The City states the first passenger train arrived at the foot of Howe Street in 1887, and that in the next seven years a building boom moved the city centre from Water and Cordova Streets up to Georgia and Granville Streets — the streets at the heart of today's VW core; streetcar service began in 1890.

The Hotel Georgia residences start where the old hotel's crown ends. The 156 Private Residences begin on floor 14, just above the crown of the 1927 Hotel Georgia, and run to a penthouse that is the entire 48th floor — a unit's floor determines whether it sits in the historic hotel's podium shadow or the glass spire above it.
Two of the core's best-known towers are deliberately filed elsewhere.

The VW core has a hospital but no confirmed core elementary. St. Paul's Hospital at 1081 Burrard Street is a genuine in-area amenity on the Burrard corridor, while the two Downtown elementaries sit at the area's south and east edges and no secondary school inside the area was confirmed — family buyers should run the VSB locator before assuming anything.

Tate's townhouses hide at the base of a 40-storey tower. The Tate Downtown development includes ground-oriented townhouse units (documented at 513 – 1283 Howe Street) inside a 333-unit strata whose manager records completion in 2018 — a buyer who filters searches to "townhouse" only, or to "apartment" only, sees only part of one development.

No park, community centre or pool in the VW core was confirmed by name on a City page in the research pass — the Coal Harbour Community Centre sits in the separate Coal Harbour sub-area and the West End's facilities sit in a separate local area, so neither is claimed here; the Central Library at 350 West Georgia Street is the core's confirmed civic anchor.

The archive framing "Downtown West Vancouver" is WRONG — West Vancouver is a different municipality. The City of Vancouver has only ONE Downtown local area, one of its 22 distinct areas; "VW" is a board/site distinction, not a City one.
Streets, schools and getting around Downtown VW

items.t: Where the housing stock concentrates: almost entirely strata apartment form in towers above and beside the business district; detached houses are not a VW-core housing form, and townhouse-form units exist mainly as ground-oriented units at tower bases.

Schools: SD39 catchments are address-based in the VSB School Locator; SD39 has no middle-school tier — elementary is Kindergarten to Grade 7 and secondary is Grades 8 to 12. The VSB directory lists two elementaries under Downtown — Elsie Roy Elementary, 150 Drake Street, and Crosstown šxʷwəq̓ʷəθət Elementary, 55 Expo Boulevard — both at the area's south and east sides (Yaletown / Crosstown), not in the VW core; an elementary school in the VW core itself, and a public secondary school inside the Downtown local area: UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Downtown VW

items.t: There is no strata townhouse complex to diligence here — the diligence is tower diligence: A Downtown VW ground-oriented unit is a strata lot in an apartment tower, so the full apartment-strata package governs: Form B Information Certificate under Strata Property Act s. 59 — monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. In the core's hotel-mixed tower (Private Residences at Hotel Georgia) the Form B is also where the residential strata's separation from the hotel and office components shows.

Property tax calendar and additional school tax: City of Vancouver 2026 advance taxes were due February 3, 2026 and main taxes July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after each due date; the home owner grant was also due July 3, 2026. At VW-core price points the Province's additional school tax can apply — 0.2% on the residential portion of assessed value between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% on the portion above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

Presales (REDMA), where a Downtown VW presale is bought: the buyer must receive the developer's disclosure statement (REDMA s. 18) and has a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing or acknowledging it (REDMA s. 21), with deposits in trust. No verified Downtown VW presale is carried in, so this is the standing frame only.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Downtown VW
Fee-simple lots

items.t: No fee-simple house-lot stock exists to document in the VW core: the Downtown District (DD) schedule of Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 governs much of the core — the only permitted uses are those in the Downtown District Official Development Plan, including commercial, residential, institutional and light industrial uses, parks and open spaces, and public uses, with development permits approved by the Development Permit Board or the Director of Planning as the schedule states; CD-1 comprehensive development districts and C-3A districts also apply in parts of the area. The tenure position is overwhelmingly strata condominium form, with rental apartment buildings and hotel and office strata also in the mix; a sourced unit-count split by tenure is UNVERIFIED.

Lot character — district position, as the schedules state them: VW-core parcels are governed by the DD, CD-1 and C-3A districts rather than house-lot minimums — C-3A shows no minimum site area for its listed uses, and a minimum lot size figure for DD or CD-1 parcels is UNVERIFIED; CD-1 districts are site-specific, so the parcel's own CD-1 bylaw states what its land can hold.
Serviced position: homes here are on City water and sewer services, as fully urban serviced stock; a 2026 utility dollar figure for a downtown home confirmed on a City source is UNVERIFIED.

ALR vs non-ALR: ALR land inside the area: UNVERIFIED in the research — no ALR parcel is documented, and no ALR percentage split is stated. Parcel-level floodplain status is likewise UNVERIFIED; the City's designated floodplain includes the False Creek coastal floodplain, and land in the floodplain is subject to the Vancouver Building By-law Floodplain Standards and Requirements for shoreline setbacks and flood construction levels — the VW core's Burrard Inlet shoreline is the edge to check against that dataset.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Downtown VW

items.t: Downtown VW is the Vancouver West board side of the City of Vancouver's official "Downtown" local area — one of the City's 22 distinct areas — covering the central business district and the Georgia / Granville / Burrard / Robson core on Burrard Inlet's south shore. The City describes Downtown as a peninsula, bounded by Burrard Inlet on the north, False Creek and the district of Yaletown to the south, the West End neighbourhood and Stanley Park to the west, and the historic districts of Gastown, Chinatown and Strathcona to the east; the VW core within it is the central and western part of that peninsula. A board-published boundary for Downtown VW alone is UNVERIFIED, as is the exact VW/VE dividing street.

Nearby areas: West End (west), Yaletown and False Creek (south), Coal Harbour (north-west waterfront), Gastown / Strathcona (east), and Mount Pleasant and Fairview (south, across False Creek). Coal Harbour towers and Yaletown buildings belong to their own sub-area files and are not claimed here.

Civic anchors in the VW core: Vancouver Public Library Central Library, 350 West Georgia Street; St. Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, is in Fairview. The City Downtown page states Downtown houses many arts, entertainment and sports venues and is the city's primary business district. A park, community centre or pool located in the VW core by name on a City page is UNVERIFIED — the Coal Harbour Community Centre sits in the separate Coal Harbour sub-area and the West End's facilities sit in a separate local area, so neither is claimed here. A shopping centre or grocery store name and address for the VW core verified on a City source is UNVERIFIED.

Roads and transit: West Georgia Street, Granville Street, Burrard Street and Howe Street are the core's main streets. The R5 Hastings St RapidBus terminates at Burrard Station, running to SFU Exchange via Hastings Street; route 22 runs from Burrard Station via Pender, Gore, Prior, Venables, Clark and Knight to Marine at Knight, with some trips continuing via the Knight Street Bridge to Richmond; route 50 (Waterfront Station / False Creek South) starts at Waterfront Station, the downtown hub station at the core's north-east edge, and runs via Chinatown, Granville Island and the False Creek south shore to Olympic Village Station. The core is the hub where the Expo Line, Millennium Line and Canada Line meet. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Schools: SD39 catchments are address-based and checked in the VSB School Locator / Catchment Boundaries tool; SD39 has no middle-school tier (elementary K–7, secondary 8–12). The VSB neighbourhood directory lists two elementaries under Downtown — Elsie Roy Elementary, 150 Drake Street, and Crosstown šxʷwəq̓ʷəθət Elementary, 55 Expo Boulevard — both at the area's south and east sides (Yaletown / Crosstown), not in the VW core; an elementary school located in the VW core itself, and a public secondary school located inside the Downtown local area, are UNVERIFIED.

All market figures: UNVERIFIED. A Downtown- or VW-only population figure is UNVERIFIED — the City publishes community statistics for the Downtown local area and the Statistics Canada 2021 Census Profile covers the City of Vancouver as a whole; neither was read as a VW figure here.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Downtown VW

items.t: Zoning — Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575, Downtown District (DD) schedule: the DD position in, with CD-1 and C-3A districts also applying in parts of the area.
Subdivision — Vancouver Subdivision By-law No. 5208 (fees under By-law No. 14538)

SSMUH / house-lot density: not a Downtown form — there are no house lots to densify; added residential capacity in the core runs through DD / CD-1 development permits, not small-scale multi-unit rules.

Floodplain standards: land in the City's designated floodplain is subject to the Vancouver Building By-law Floodplain Standards and Requirements for shoreline setbacks and flood construction levels; whether a specific VW-core parcel is in the floodplain is UNVERIFIED — check the parcel against the City's designated-floodplain dataset.

Strata block (the operative tenure block for this ground): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw. For strata purchases, review the depreciation report, contingency reserve and any special levies before pricing an offer; BC strata disputes can go to the Civil Resolution Tribunal.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Downtown VW ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

Empty Homes Tax — VANCOUVER ONLY, applies here: Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax is 3% of assessed value for vacant properties; every Vancouver owner must submit an annual property status declaration (due February 3, 2026), and the 2025 Empty Homes Tax payment was due April 16, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after that date — a standing check on any VW-core purchase, where investor-held units are common.

City of Vancouver property taxes + additional school tax: 2026 advance taxes were due February 3, 2026 and main taxes were due July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after each due date; the home owner grant was also due July 3, 2026. At VW-core price points the additional school tax can apply — 0.2% on the residential portion between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

blocks.text: Good to know about Downtown VW

items.t: The core's street pattern is dated City record: the City states the first passenger train arrived at the foot of Howe Street in 1887, a year after incorporation, and that in the next seven years a building boom moved the city centre from Water and Cordova Streets up to Georgia and Granville Streets — the streets at the heart of today's VW core; streetcar service began in 1890.

The in-area hospital is not a VCH hospital: St. Paul's Hospital, 1081 Burrard Street, is a Providence Health Care hospital — which is why the batch-5 downtown-ve research, checking VCH pages, could not confirm an in-area hospital. Citing VCH for St.

The archive title for this ground is wrong, on the record: the website archive's "Downtown West Vancouver" title belongs to no municipality — this ground is Downtown Vancouver, and West Vancouver's bylaws, taxes and pricing must never be imported into a downtown listing.

The additional school tax steps up on a fixed date: the rates that apply at Downtown price points (0.2% / 0.4%) rise to 0.3% / 0.6% on January 1, 2027 — a closing that straddles that date carries two different tax years' math on the same assessment.
The published CMHC range is 0.6%–4.5%.

Page-statement check for this area. Approved page claims, where a live page states them, are the settled set only: REALTOR since 2015; 10 straight years in the FVREB Medallion Club; Top 1% of Fraser Valley Realtors; #1 in South Surrey/White Rock by MLS points for 2025 and 2026 YTD; more than $500M in sales.

faq.q: Is Coal Harbour or Yaletown part of Downtown VW?
faq.a: They sit inside or beside the Downtown local area but are their own Paragon sub-areas with their own pages — Coal Harbour has its own file in this batch — so their buildings and plans are not part of this page.

faq.q: Which hospital is inside the area?
faq.a: St. Paul's Hospital, 1081 Burrard Street, on the Burrard corridor in the VW core; it is a Providence Health Care hospital. Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, is in Fairview, south across False Creek.

faq.q: Which transit terminates in the VW core?
faq.a: The R5 Hastings St RapidBus terminates at Burrard Station, route 22 also runs from Burrard Station, and route 50 starts at Waterfront Station — the core is the hub where the Expo Line, Millennium Line and Canada Line meet.

faq.q: Can Jared show me homes in Downtown VW?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Downtown VW condo long-term?
faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, whatever a directory line says. Short-term rentals are a separate question: stratas can still restrict them and Vancouver licences them. The Empty Homes Tax declaration applies if the unit sits empty instead.

faq.q: Which schools serve a VW-core address?
faq.a: SD39 catchments are address-based. The VSB directory lists two elementaries under Downtown — Elsie Roy (150 Drake Street) and Crosstown šxʷwəq̓ʷəθət (55 Expo Boulevard) — both at the area's south and east sides, not in the VW core; an elementary in the core itself and a public secondary inside the Downtown local area: UNVERIFIED.

faq.q: Why do sources disagree on Tate Downtown's completion year and 1188 Howe's size?
faq.a: Tate's strata manager records construction completed and opened in 2018 while current listings record built 2019; 1188 Howe's directory records 185 residential plus 5 commercial units in its description and 190 units in its FAQ, with built 1994 in one line and 1995 in another. Both conflicts are flagged in — the strata plan and depreciation report are the settling documents.

faq.q: A listing calls a Tate unit a "townhouse." What am I actually buying?
faq.a: A strata lot in a 333-unit apartment tower (Tate Downtown, 1283 Howe Street) — the documented unit, 513 – 1283 Howe Street, is a 3-storey townhouse-form lot at the tower's base, Freehold Strata. Built form governs: your strata is the tower, with its depreciation report, CRF and levy history.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Downtown VW unit long-term?
faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since Nov 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, whatever a directory line says. Short-term rentals are a separate question: stratas can still restrict them and Vancouver licences them. The Empty Homes Tax declaration applies if the unit sits empty instead.

faq.q: What is the Empty Homes Tax hit if I leave a VW-core home empty?
faq.a: 3% of assessed value for a property deemed vacant, on top of the annual declaration duty — Vancouver only; the City's 2025 annual report describes the 3% rate as consistent and stable. The provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax is a separate filing.

faq.q: Is Downtown VW a different neighbourhood from Downtown VE?
faq.a: No — the City has one Downtown local area among its 22 distinct areas; VW and VE are the board/site split of that one area, with this page covering the west-side core. The exact board dividing street is UNVERIFIED — do not state Main Street or Ontario Street as the line without a board source.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot or a house lot downtown?
faq.a: No — detached houses are not a VW-core housing form, no bare-land or bare-land-strata stock was verified, and downtown land trades as strata units, airspace and development rights inside DD / CD-1 / C-3A parcels.
